core_obligations: Set up the criterion (proof lines 4089-4108): let B be the set of affine objects U of the pro-etale site of X with the structure ring ind-etale over the ring of X, and let Cov be the set of pro-etale coverings between them; conditions (1) and (2) of the Cech vanishing criterion hold by the permanence and base change lemmas for ind-etale algebras and the description of the pro-etale topology on an affine scheme.

Reduce a pro-etale covering to etale coverings (proof lines 4110-4132): given a covering in Cov write each U_i as a directed inverse limit of affine etale U_{i,a} over U; limits commute with fibre products, so the Cech complex of the covering is the filtered colimit of the Cech complexes of the etale coverings U_{(a_1,...,a_n)}, and by exactness of filtered colimits it suffices to prove the vanishing for etale coverings of U.

Approximate an etale covering from below (proof lines 4134-4155): for an etale covering with affine U_i, write U as a directed inverse limit of affine etale U_b over X and use the limit descent lemmas to spread the covering out to a genuine etale covering U_b for large b; the Cech complex of the given covering is then the filtered colimit of the Cech complexes of the coverings U_b, and those complexes of the pullback agree with the complexes of the original injective sheaf by the comparison and limit lemmas.

Conclude (proof lines 4155-4163): the Cech complexes of an injective sheaf over an etale covering are acyclic in positive degrees, hence so is their filtered colimit, which verifies condition (3); since X itself is one of the objects of B, the criterion gives the vanishing of H^p(X_proetale, epsilon^{-1}I) for p > 0.
proof_roadmap: Choose the building blocks and coverings for which the pro-etale Cech complex can be compared with etale ones.
Write a pro-etale covering as a filtered colimit of etale coverings.
Approximate a general etale covering of a pro-etale object by etale coverings of an etale approximation of that object.
Conclude by the acyclicity of the Cech complex of an injective sheaf and the criterion.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for an affine scheme X and an injective abelian sheaf I on the small etale site, the higher pro-etale cohomology of the pullback of I vanishes (statement lines 4082-4087). The proof (proof lines 4089-4167) applies the Cech vanishing criterion: it verifies conditions (1) and (2) for a suitable set of affine objects and coverings, reduces pro-etale coverings to filtered colimits of etale coverings, approximates an etale covering by etale coverings of an etale approximation of the base, and concludes by the acyclicity of the Cech complex of an injective sheaf. H3: an original reduction of pro-etale coverings to etale ones combined with a limit approximation, all written out in full.
